item.title: Re: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded: Thanks for the critique! Yeah, I definitely need to dig a little deeper and think about what makes this idea tick. There's something in there that made me want to write this idea, but it's kind of unclear. Back to the drawing board!

item.title: Re: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
Hello there! I saw 'Collective Unconscious' and I just…had to swing by and give my thoughts.

So.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

First, the Elevator Pitch. I want to like it, what with the imagery of a tree and its root connecting to and reaching throughout all of humanity's subconscious and such, but so far, all it does is just…make people see it in their heads and then make them feel dread.

As for the Central Narrative, I'm similarly not very impressed.

The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

This feels tacked on and like it was added solely to attempt to add a sense of mystery and nothing else. It's never elaborated upon and it's mentioned and dropped immediately.

There are also some bits that contradict each other.

the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread,

I like this bit, but other than the imagery of roots that obviously allude to burrowing throughout the Collective Unconscious, this, too, fails to go anywhere.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.

If it's meant to be scary or unsettling, then why dread?

The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

Unfortunately, it is very overt.

And that ends my crit. I do apologize if this was overly harsh.

There's some neat imagery in here, but sadly, not much else to go off of.

In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

This sentence alone was my favorite part of this entire forum post. Especialy 'dread' and 'like an unobtainable goal' got my attention.

I recommend peeking a little more into Carl Jung's studies on psychoanalysis if you really want to make an SCP based off a symbol in the Collective Unconscious.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day! :D

item.title: Re: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
Hey! Thank you so much! First of all, I didn't know of the term "noosphere", so you've introduced me to some new reading material. Second, thanks for linking me to that guide. I think you're right about the complexity, and I should focus on adding more depth to the idea.

As for the nature of the anomaly, I'm going to be honest in saying that I wasn't really thinking about the tree as a symbol of tranquility as much as it being a rather mundane object. However, I think I can see some potential for irony given this symbolism. I definitely will give this more thought.

item.title: Re: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Please note that I am not the most experienced user and am not qualified to give Greenlights. Please reach out to veteran authors and critters for some more informed crit.

here's the crit
wow look at that

I find the basic tenets of this idea very intriguing. The idea of a bonsai tree infecting the noosphere (collective human thought) is suitably mysterious and has great imagery potential. However, I believe that you'll find more success, both in the idea forums and the mainlist, if you can simplify your idea as much as possible. When I was having similar issues, this guide helped a lot: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/yourjouney-part-1

Another issue I have is that the exact nature of this anomaly seems to be a bit shaky. Here are some questions that I have that might inspire the development process:
Bonsai trees typically represent peace or tranquillity. What causes this one to be a symbol of the exact opposite?
There are multiple issues with the entire world instantly becoming aware of this phenomenon. What if everyone has this image in their minds, but cannot place it and typically don't pay it much mind?
Bonsai trees are tightly controlled by their gardeners to take on certain shapes and inspire certain feelings. What does the nature of this tree say about the person who grew it?

Overall, I believe this has promise. If you receive the necessary greenlights, please reach out to me with a draft. Have a good day!

item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in some apartment in Iran.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in an abandoned apartment in Iran.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation is compelled to visit an apartment that everybody, including other agencies concerned with the anomalous, seemed to know about. It turns out that the anomaly is not the apartment itself, but a bonsai tree sitting in the bedroom. The Foundation takes over the entire apartment complex, "managing" it to keep appearances. The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

+ show block
– hide block

They find out that the bonsai tree emits radio signals through an invisible root system throughout the Earth. These radio signals cause those exposed to them for prolonged periods to feel intense dread and regret. Not much else learned about the bonsai tree, and the former tenant is still at large.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Knowledge of an object suddenly enters the collective unconscious.

Additional Notes: What I really want to highlight is the juxtaposition between the ubiquity of the bonsai tree within the collective unconscious and the anonymity of the original tenant. In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

While drafting this idea, I kept having trouble with suggesting the meaning of the tree's radio signals and the significance of the date in which it manifested. The idea is that the tree sort of feeds off of people's anxieties, and the "root system" connects to the minds of every person on Earth. The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
